earlier.claim: status() reads folderVersion (and the staged copy) instead of the version claude lists, so the install post-check always equals cli_version and is dead. After a kmctl upgrade, `kmctl plugin install` exits 0 and reports plugin 0.2.0 while `claude plugin list --json` shows kmctl@kmctl at version 0.1.0 with only the 0.1.0 cache dir, and `kmctl plugin status` reports no problem.

install() skips adding scaccogatto when any scope already knows it, so a project-scope install in a second repo, or for a user who already has scaccogatto at user scope, writes enabledPlugins okf@scaccogatto to .claude/settings.json with no extraKnownMarketplaces entry for scaccogatto. The plan says the project settings file lists both marketplaces.

_listed() returns the first kmctl@kmctl entry, whatever its scope or projectPath. claude lists project-scope installs from other repos (enabled false), so in a repo with no install, status reports 'version mismatch ... run kmctl plugin update' from another repo's entry instead of 'not installed; run kmctl plugin install'. The install post-check can also read the wrong entry.

r1's test never checks that the kmctl and okf entries are at the chosen scope, though fails_when says 'at that scope'. r2's test compares only kmctl's version, not the whole plugin list as fails_when says, and never checks the first install's exit code.

_report is typed `result: object`, so mypy reports 4 new errors (asdict overload and attr-defined at __init__.py:485-490). It should take PluginStatus. Two older mypy errors remain (review_due.py:120, __init__.py:318).

new.claim: No test covers the f1 fix: a plain install over an older installed version must exit 1 naming kmctl plugin update, and status must report the installed-version mismatch. r5's test only edits the staged copy, so it passes even if the installed-version check is removed.
